description: Run a scene in Godot 4.7 headless for some physics frames with an input timeline, and return a table of the watched values per frame plus errors and prints. Each input lands on exactly that physics frame and runs are deterministic. `input` steps: a frame, a verb (press, release, tap, or hold with a frame count) and an action or event such as Key:Space. `watch`: a node path from the scene root, a dot, then a property or method call. `until` stops at the first frame a condition holds; `signals` records when signals fire, with their arguments; `summary: true` gives one line per watched value (start, end, min, max, first change), cheaper on long runs; `expect` claims ("Heli.health > 0", "Heli.position.y < 1 @ 90", or how often a recorded signal fired) make the result an error when one fails, so a run doubles as a test; keep a passing run with godot_scenario op save and the same arguments. An error result when the run does not finish or Godot reports an error; an unknown input action is a warning. Project files are not changed (it runs a temporary script in .godot/godotwright/). For tests kept in the project use godot_test; for load errors godot_check.

every.description: sample every n frames (default 10); frames with input and the last frame are always sampled

expect.description: claims to check: "Heli.health > 0" (last frame) or "Heli.position.y < 1 @ 90"; their values are watched; on a recorded signal, "Heli.landed >= 1" counts how often it fired

input.description: timeline: "10 press jump; 30 release jump; 40 hold right 20; 50 tap Key:Space"

path.description: project folder, or a file or folder inside it (relative to the server's folder; default: the current project)

scene.description: the res:// scene to run (default: the main scene)

summary.description: one line per watched value instead of a table (samples every frame)

until.description: stop at the first frame where this holds: "Heli.is_on_floor() == true"

watch.description: values to sample: Player.position, Player.velocity.y, Player.is_on_floor()

name: godot_play
title: Play a scene with input
